about.title: How this is drawn
about.p1: Read a closed curve as a complex function z(t) = x(t) + i·y(t), t ∈ [0, 1); it can be written z(t) = Σ c_k·e^{2πikt}. Each term is a circle of radius |c_k| that turns k times per cycle (counter-clockwise for positive k, clockwise for negative) from the starting angle arg(c_k). Chain the circles end to end and the pen on the last one draws the line.
about.p2: Finitely many circles are always an approximation. As the number of circles goes to infinity, the partial sums converge uniformly to the curve, as long as it is continuous and of finite length (the Dirichlet–Jordan theorem).
about.p3: How fast depends on how smooth the curve is: on a curve that is smooth everywhere the coefficients fall off quickly; with sharp corners |c_k| falls off only like 1/k², so with too few circles the corners get rounded and straight edges ripple.
about.p4: The coefficients here are the discrete Fourier transform of N points taken at equal arc length along the line. With all N − 1 circles the curve passes through every one of those points; ordered by size, any number of circles gives the smallest RMS error possible with that many.
about.keys: Space: play / pause. ← / →: fewer or more circles (with Shift, one at a time). D: draw your own. Esc: cancel drawing or the demo.
